text.p: Independence Hall and surrounding buildings have been ordered closed for a week because construction crews stirred up asbestos dust, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Thursday.

About 2,500 tourists a day will be limited to walking around the exterior of Independence Hall, where the Founding Fathers met to draft both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution more than 200 years ago.
National Park Service officials said it was unlikely that earlier tourists had been exposed, since prior tests had not detected any asbestos dust.
Asbestos dust is known to be a cause of cancer.

According to the newspaper, the workers were in the basement of Congress Hall, built in 1789 for the city courts but used by both houses of the new national legislature between 1790 and 1800. Because the dust was detected in neighbouring Independence Hall too, the central structure in the complex of buildings also was closed.

Park Service officials said the refurbishing work being done by the construction crews would be completed in time for the complex to play a role in the Summit on America's Future later this month, the newpaper said.
The event, supported by President Clinton and scheduled to start April 27, has no events planned for inside the buildings.
